note: Fuzzer receives raw input bytes; first 6 bytes are config (color format, cores, arch), remaining bytes are the H.264/MVC bitstream passed to the decoder.
Header decode phase processes SPS/PPS NAL units; SEI NAL units are skipped during header decode because ih264d_parse_nal_unit only calls ih264d_parse_sei_message when !ps_dec->i4_decode_header.
Frame decode phase begins; the bitstream containing the SEI NAL unit with film grain characteristics is passed to the MVC decoder.
The SEI NAL unit (type 6) is not an MVC NAL, so it is dispatched to ih264d_parse_nal_unit for standard AVC NAL processing.
The NAL unit type is SEI (6); since this is frame decode mode (i4_decode_header is 0), the code proceeds to parse the SEI message.
Converts RBSP to SODB by removing trailing stop bit and padding; the bitstream buffer is set up with the NAL payload.
Calls SEI message parser which reads payload type and payload size from the bitstream.
Reads the SEI payload type; for film grain characteristics, payload type is 19 (SEI_FILM_GRAIN_CHARACTERISTICS).
Reads the SEI payload size; this value is used to check bit sufficiency before calling the payload parser.
Checks that ui4_payload_size*8 bits are available in the bitstream; this check passes for a small payload size, but does not account for the excessive bits read by ih264d_parse_fgc.
Dispatches to the film grain characteristics parser since payload type is 19.
The payload type matches SEI_FILM_GRAIN_CHARACTERISTICS (19), so ih264d_parse_fgc is called.
Captures the raw bitstream buffer pointer; this buffer has limited size based on the NAL unit length, and reads beyond it will cause heap-buffer-overflow.
Reads the cancel flag; set to 0 so the parser continues into the film grain parameter fields.
Reads film grain model id; set to 0 to pass the validation check (must be <= 1).
Reads separate colour description flag; set to 0 so the parser uses SPS bit depths (requires ps_cur_sps to be non-NULL).
Reads blending mode id; set to 0 to pass validation (must be <= 1).
Reads log2 scale factor (4 bits).
Reads 3 component model present flags; set all to 1 so the parser enters the nested loops for all colour components.
Reads num_intensity_intervals_minus1 (8 bits, up to 255); set to a large value like 255 to maximize the number of iterations in the inner loop.
Reads num_model_values_minus1 (3 bits, up to 7); set to 7 to maximize iterations in the innermost loop.
Outer loop iterates up to 256 times (when num_intensity_intervals_minus1=255); each iteration reads 16 bits for bounds plus sev values in the inner loop.
Reads 8 bits for lower bound; with 256 iterations across 3 components, this consumes 6144 bits just for bounds.
Reads 8 bits for upper bound; continues consuming bits far beyond the declared payload size.
Inner loop iterates up to 8 times per intensity interval; each iteration calls ih264d_sev which reads variable-length Exp-Golomb coded values.
Calls ih264d_sev which reads Exp-Golomb signed values; each call advances the bitstream offset and reads from pu4_bitstrm_buf without bounds checking against the actual NAL payload size.

The bitstream offset advances far beyond the allocated buffer size. With 3 components × 256 intervals × 8 model values, the parser attempts to read thousands of bits from a buffer that only contains the small SEI payload.
GETBITS macro reads a 32-bit word from the bitstream buffer at the computed word offset; when u4_ofst exceeds the buffer size, this reads out of bounds causing heap-buffer-overflow READ of 4 bytes.
When the bit offset crosses a 32-bit word boundary, the macro also reads the next word; if u4_word_off+1 is beyond the allocated buffer, this causes an additional out-of-bounds read.

The ih264d_sev function internally calls ih264d_get_bits_h264 via the GETBITS macro; with the bitstream offset pushed far beyond the buffer end by the nested loops, the macro reads from invalid memory, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow READ of 4 bytes.
